name: Weekly AI digest with real sources to a WordPress draft

parameters.content:
### Any chat model works

Gemini Flash is here because this pattern was built to survive a free tier. Swap in OpenAI, Anthropic or a local model and nothing else changes.

Keep the temperature low. This is a summarising job, not a creative one.

## 4 · Enforce the limits, then draft

Asking a model to count characters is asking the wrong tool, and it fails silently — you find out when the search result is already truncated. **Enforce Output Limits** trims the title and excerpt on a word boundary instead. It also refuses to draft an empty post: a failed execution is legible, an empty draft in the CMS looks like a decision somebody made.

Markdown To HTML exists because WordPress wants HTML, not markdown.

**Swapping the destination:** replace the last node only. Everything upstream is CMS-agnostic and hands on a clean `title`, `excerpt`, `body` and `tags` — use Notion, Ghost, or an HTTP Request to your own API.

**On tags:** the WordPress node wants term *IDs*, not names, so the model’s tags are not attached. Add them at review time.

## 3 · Collate, then write once

Collate flattens both result sets, drops duplicate URLs and numbers them into one citable block. The same link listed twice reads to a model as two corroborating sources.

**Why this is a chain and not an agent.** The obvious build gives an agent a search tool and lets it decide what to look for. That cost one model call per iteration and took seven of them — impossible against a five-a-minute limit.

Grounding got **stronger**, not weaker: with findings pasted into the prompt, the model can only cite URLs in front of it.

## 2 · Two searches, fixed

Two plain HTTP calls to SerpAPI. Keep the queries genuinely different from each other — two phrasings of the same question return the same links and waste a call.

`tbs=qdr:w` scopes results to the past week deterministically, so the model never has to reason about what "this week" means.

**`executeOnce` is on for Search Two.** Chained after Search One, it would otherwise run once per incoming item.

Both retry 3× on failure, so a transient 5xx does not cost you the week.

## 1 · Trigger and settings

Fires once a week. Weekly rather than daily is deliberate: a daily digest of a field that moves weekly is a digest of noise.

**Config is the only node you edit.** It holds both search queries, the freshness window, how many results to pull, and one line describing who reads the digest — that line lands in the system prompt and is what keeps the output from reading like a press release.

Everything downstream reads its settings from here, so there is no second place to remember.

# Weekly AI digest, with sources it actually retrieved

Every Friday this searches the web for the past seven days, writes a digest that can **only** cite the links it was given, and files it as a **draft** for a person to review. Nothing is ever published automatically.

**Setup, about five minutes:** add a **SerpAPI** credential to both search nodes · a **chat model** credential to *Digest Model* · a **WordPress** credential to *Create Draft* · then edit the two queries in **Config**. That node is the only thing you need to change.

**What it costs to run:** 2 search calls and 1 model call per successful run — 8 searches a month, or 24 in the worst case where every call exhausts its 3 retries. Both sit inside SerpAPI’s free 100. The trigger fires 07:00 in **your instance’s timezone**; set that in Settings, or change the trigger.

parameters.jsonSchemaExample: { "title": "What actually shipped in AI this week", "excerpt": "One sentence on the through-line.", "body": "Markdown with ## per item and a source link in each.", "tags": ["ai", "weekly"] }

parameters.text:
=Today is {{ $now.toFormat('d MMMM yyyy') }}. Write this week's digest.

Below are {{ $json.count }} search results from the past seven days. They are the ONLY material you may cite. Use the exact URLs given.

=== SEARCH RESULTS ===
{{ $json.findings }}
=== END ===

Pick the two or three items that genuinely matter to the reader described in your instructions. Ignore anything that is an advert, a listicle, a funding round or an executive move.

If none of the results describe a real development from this week, say so plainly in a short post rather than inventing substance. A quiet week is an acceptable outcome and an honest one.

messageValues.message:
=You write a weekly digest for {{ $('Config').first().json.audience }}.

Non-negotiable: every item must come from a search result you were given. Include the source URL as a markdown link in that item. If you cannot find a real source for something, leave it out. Never state a version number, benchmark, price or date you did not see in the results.

Structure:
- One short opening paragraph naming the through-line of the week. No preamble, no "welcome back".
- ## per item. The heading states what changed, not the product name alone.
- Each item: what happened, the source link, then a short paragraph headed by "Why it matters for building:" giving a practical read — what you would do differently, what you would not adopt yet, what it breaks.
- Close with one honest line on what you are watching next.

Voice: plain, direct, first person for the opinion parts. No hype, no "game-changer", no "the landscape is shifting". Sceptical by default — if something is overhyped, say so.

700 to 1100 words. Markdown only.

Return only the structured object: title, excerpt, body, tags.
- title: name the week's actual through-line; do not prefix every week with the same boilerplate.
- excerpt: one sentence. It becomes the meta description.
- tags: three to five, lowercase, always including the main subject.

Keep the title and excerpt short. They are trimmed downstream if they run long, and a trimmed title reads worse than one you kept tight yourself.
